item.title: Trump says he's banning CNN, Politico and MS NOW from the White House
item.description: President Trump said Friday that he is banning CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the White House, the latest move to target media outlets over their reporting.

item.title: Major Garrett argues "Trump is signaling he's weak" with ban on CNN, MS NOW and Politico
item.description: President Trump lashed out at reporters who cover his administration on Friday, saying he would ban CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the White House. Major Garrett shares his thoughts on the ban and CBS News senior White House correspondent Weijia Jiang reports.

item.title: Trump says he's banning CNN, MS NOW and Politico from White House
item.description: President Trump took questions from reporters on Friday after he said he was banning CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the White House. CBS News correspondent Natalie Brand and legal contributor Jessica Levinson have more.

item.title: This week on "Sunday Morning" (Sept. 20)
item.description: A look at the features for this week's broadcast of the Emmy-winning program, hosted by Jane Pauley.

item.title: Mortgage rates are nearing 7%. One house hunter says he's "despondent."
item.description: "It seems like we're trying to climb out of a hole somebody else is digging," said one frustrated house hunter as homeownership costs rise.

item.title: Book excerpt: "Go and Do Likewise" by Andy Beshear
item.description: The Democratic Governor of Kentucky writes about how the language of faith, which he believes has been co-opted by some politicians, can be used to bridge the nation's partisan divide.

item.title: RFK Jr. tells anti-vaccine activists they have a "friend in the White House"
item.description: Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. spoke at a conference hosted by an organization he once led that has promoted doubts about vaccines.

item.title: "Face the Nation with Margaret Brennan" guests for Sept. 20, 2026
item.description: This week's guests include Republican Sen. Bill Cassidy of Louisiana, Democratic Rep. Ro Khanna of California and Republican Rep. Maria Salazar of Florida.

item.title: DOJ says ban on selling handguns to young adults under 21 is unconstitutional
item.description: The Justice Department released a new legal opinion that concludes a federal law prohibiting firearms dealers from selling handguns to people between the ages of 18 and 20 is unconstitutional.

item.title: Feds plan to transfer hundreds of pre-trial detainees in private prison dispute
item.description: The U.S. Marshals Service is preparing to transfer some Georgia detainees to another private facility 200 miles away.

item.title: Trump orders DOJ not to fight ruling that loosened limits on "gangster weapons," sources say
item.description: President Trump has ordered the Justice Department not to appeal a court ruling that loosened restrictions on firearms known as "gangster weapons." CBS News' Sarah Lynch reports.

item.title: Early voting for midterm elections begin in some states
item.description: Early in-person voting has begun in Virginia, Minnesota and South Dakota for this year's midterm elections. CBS News' Shawna Mizelle reports.

item.title: 2 ships attacked in Strait of Hormuz as Trump grapples with his next move
item.description: Following more attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz, Trump said he'll make a "big decision" on whether to "annihilate" Iran's leadership.

item.title: Increased ICE enforcement in 2025 hurt local employment, analysis finds
item.description: Employment fell last year in U.S. cities where ICE arrests surged, according to the Brookings Institution.

item.title: Police capture suspected serial killer disguised as woman, carrying baby
item.description: Brazilian police said they will reopen dozens of cases linked to a self-confessed serial killer who was arrested as he attempted to escape dressed as a woman and carrying a baby.

item.title: Trump to sign Russia sanctions bill today, source says
item.description: President Trump will sign the recently passed Russia sanctions bill Friday, a White House official tells CBS News. CBS News' Weijia Jiang has more on that and the rest of the news coming out of the White House.

item.title: AI agent Claude is building the next version of itself, Anthropic says
item.description: Anthropic says AI agent Claude is building the next version of itself as industry experts continue to sound alarms about the technology's potential power and risks. Journalist and author Sebastian Mallaby joins CBS News to discuss his new op-ed saying calls by Anthropic co-founder Dario Amodei to slow down AI development don't go far enough.

item.title: Grandmother falsely accused of bank fraud sues Fargo, North Dakota, over AI facial recognition
item.description: A Tennessee grandmother is suing the city of Fargo, North Dakota, after facial recognition software linked her to a crime she didn't commit, which led to a nearly six-month stay in jail. CBS News' Nicole Valdes has more.

item.title: Unpacking GOP Rep. Salazar's ad blasting Trump's immigration policies
item.description: Only six weeks remain before Americans vote in November's midterm elections. CBS News' Zak Hudak has the latest political headlines.

item.title: Flights are only going to get more expensive so book your holiday tickets now, expert says
item.description: Travel costs are up as fuel prices soar. The Points Guys managing editor Clint Henderson shares his cost saving tips.

item.title: Uber ordered to pay $40 million in wrongful death suit
item.description: A woman was hit and killed after an Uber driver forced her and her friend out of his car on a freeway. Now, Uber has been ordered to pay $40 million after the victim's family brought forth a wrongful death suit. CBS News' Lauren Pozen reports.

item.title: Trump's next move could be to "annihilate" Iran, he tells Axios
item.description: President Trump told Axios that his next move could be to "annihilate" Iran. CBS News' Aaron Navarro reports.

item.title: Use of AI backfires on an expert witness at trial: "They have biases"
item.description: The use of artificial intelligence in the courtroom is drawing fresh attention after an expert witness in a multimillion-dollar lawsuit used ChatGPT to help create his report.

item.title: Duncan Sheik, singer-songwriter of "Barely Breathing," dies at 56
item.description: Duncan Sheik died on Thursday night, his family said.

item.title: Twins conjoined at the head are separated in 25-hour surgery
item.description: The twins were born in Ethiopia with a rare condition that left them joined at the head. Doctors spent a year planning a separation surgery.

item.title: Holdout juror in Lindsay Clancy trial says he "didn't have any doubts"
item.description: Michael Desronvil, the lone holdout juror in the high-profile Lindsay Clancy murder trial, said he "didn't have any doubts" during deliberations.

item.title: Senator urges Trump to press Xi on Chinese info Iran may be using to target troops
item.description: Democratic Sen. Elissa Slotkin urged President Trump to make this issue a "centerpiece of your talks with President Xi."

item.title: Sacramento Sikh truck driver survives being stabbed 17 times at Wyoming rest stop
item.description: A Sacramento Sikh truck driver was stabbed 17 times in an unprovoked attack at a Wyoming truck stop on Sunday, his attorney says.

item.title: GOP congresswoman says Trump immigration enforcement has "gone too far"
item.description: "The same Hispanics who helped you get to the White House in 2024 feel betrayed," said Rep. Maria Elvira Salazar.

item.title: Senate Democrats meet with El-Sayed, rallying around Michigan nominee
item.description: Michigan Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed met with Senate Democrats as they look to rally around his candidacy in the final sprint to November's election.
